s: If Kidneys of a person are not working, he would undergo?
Artificial chemicals are bio-chemically known as
Scientists have developed an artificial muscle to treat which of the body part?
Pace-maker is related to:
x: A pacemaker is a device that regulates the heartbeat, so it is related to the heart.

s: The universal recipient blood group is
x: Blood group AB has both A and B antigens and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it is the universal recipient; O negative is the universal donor.

src: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
s: Which of the following human body organs behaves like the endocrine as well as exocrine glands?
x: The pancreas is both endocrine (insulin from Islets of Langerhans) and exocrine (digestive enzymes). Liver, testis and pituitary are not described this way.

s: Which of the following glands in humans is located on the kidney?
x: The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so the adrenal gland is the one on the kidney. The pituitary, thyroid and hypothalamus are in the brain or neck.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the functions of Glucagon?
o: Glucagon is essential for your health. It supports cell growth, immune function, fetal development and vision.
Glucagon triggers your liver to convert stored glucose (glycogen) into a usable form and then release it into your bloodstream. This process is called glycogenolysis.
Glucagon helps your body make glucose from other sources, such as amino acids.
Glucagon can also prevent your liver from taking in and storing glucose so that more glucose stays in your blood.
x: Glucagon raises blood glucose through glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis from amino acids, and reduced hepatic glucose uptake; the statement about cell growth, immunity, fetal development and vision describes vitamin A, not glucagon.

s: Which of the following glands in humans is located on the kidney?
x: The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so the adrenal gland is the one on the kidney. The pituitary, thyroid and hypothalamus are in the brain or neck.

s: Which gland in the human body continuously supplies tear fluid that is wiped across the surface of the eyes each time the eyelids are blinked?
x: The lacrimal gland secretes tear fluid that is spread over the eye by blinking. The thyroid, salivary and pituitary glands have no such role.

s: Identify functions of insulin from the following
x: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and fat storage and lowers blood sugar, including by slowing glycogen breakdown in the liver, so all of the listed functions are correct.

s: Which of the following is associated with Diabetes Mellitus?
o: High sugar level and high insulin level in blood
High sugar level and low insulin level in blood
Low sugar level and high insulin level in blood
Low sugar level and low insulin level in blood
x: In diabetes mellitus the pancreas produces insufficient insulin (or cells resist it), so glucose accumulates in the blood.

s: The largest gland in the human body is
x: The liver is the largest gland in the human body, performing vital functions such as detoxification, protein synthesis, bile production and metabolism regulation.

s: Which live-cut human organ has the ability to grow back to nearly 85 percent of its original capability within 2-3 weeks?
x: The liver is renowned for its regenerative capacity, restoring a large proportion of lost mass and function within a few weeks after partial removal.

s: Which hormone stimulates the thyroid gland to secrete thyroxine?
x: The hormonal output from the thyroid is regulated by thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) produced by the anterior pituitary.

s: Average blood pressure of a human is –
x: The normal average blood pressure of human is 120/80 mm Hg. This means that systolic pressure around 120mm Hg and diastolic pressure should be around 80 mm Hg.

s: The normal temperature of the human body is –
x: Normal human body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F). 98°C is far too high; 367 K is about 94°C, not 37°C (310 K).

s: In a patient of Thalassemia, the body is unable to synthesise –
x: Thalassemia is a genetic blood disorder. In a patient of Thalassemia, the body is unable to synthesise enough haemoglobin, which causes severe anaemia.

s: The process by which blood is purified in human body is called :
x: Dialysis is a process for removing waste and excess water from the blood and is used primarily as an artificial replacement for lost kidney function in people with kidney failure. Dialysis filters out unwanted substances and fluids from the blood. 6. 'Dialysis' is related to ? (a) Liver (b) Kidney (c) Eyes (d) Brain M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2004 Ans. (b)

s: The human eye forms the image of an object at its –
x: The eye's lens focuses light to form the image on the retina, which holds the photoreceptors. The cornea, iris and pupil do not form the image.

s: In a Sitar, which type of sound vibrations are produced?
x: When we pluck the string of an instrument, like the Sitar, the sound that we hear is not only that of the string. The whole instrument is forced to vibrate, and it is the sound of the vibration of the instrument that we hear. When a string under tension is set into vibration, a transverse wave travels along the wire and is reflected at the fixed end. A transverse stationary wave is thus formed. 6. Long radio waves are reflected by which of the following layer of Earth's surface – (a) Troposphere (b) Ionosphere (c) Tropopause (d) Stratosphere U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1991 Ans. (b) The ionosphere is a region of Earth's upper atmosphere from about 50 to 400 miles altitude. It is ionized by solar radiation. It has practical importance because among other functions, it influences radio propagation to distant places on Earth. 7. Wireless communication is reflected back to the earth’s surface by the – (a) Troposphere (b) Stratosphere (c) Ionosphere (d) Exosphere U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1998 Ans. (c)

s: Iodine containing hormone is –
x: The thyroid gland is located in the front of the neck attached to the lower part of the voice box (larynx) and to the upper part of the windpipe (trachea). The thyroid gland produces thyroid hormones-thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) . These are iodine containing hormones. Thyroid cells combine iodine and the amino acid tyrosine to make thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) hormones. T4 molecule contains four iodine atoms while T3 molecule have three iodine atoms.

s: When kidneys fail to function, there is accumulation of–
o: Nitrogenous waste products in the blood
x: Metabolism refers to all of the body's chemical process, the digestion of food and the elimination of waste. The main nitrogenous wastes are ammonia, urea and uric acid. Urea is formed from gluconeogenesis of amino acids. Urea is one of the primary components of urine. When kidneys fail to function, there is accumulation of nitrogenous waste products in the blood.

s: In human body, vitamin A is stored in –
x: Vitamin A is largely stored in the liver in the human body. Its chemical name is retinol whose deficiency causes night blindness.

s: A man having ‘A’ blood group met a serious road accident and the doctors advised for blood transfusion. The relatives were asked to donate blood, whose blood groups were found to be as follows : (i) Wife – ‘O’ (ii) Brother – ‘AB’ (iii) Son – ‘A’ (iv) Daughter – ‘O’ Who among the above relations could donate blood to the injured man?
x: Blood group A individuals have the A antigen on the surface of their RBCs and blood serum containing IgM antibodies against the B antigen. Therefore, group A individual can receive blood only from individuals of groups A or O (with A being preferable) and can donate blood to individuals with type A or AB.

s: The dialyzer is used for the work of –
x: The treatment options for kidney failure are peritoneal dialysis (PD), hemodialysis and kidney transplant. A dialyzer is an artificial kidney designed to provide controllable transfer of solutes and water across a semipermeable membrane separating flowing blood and dialysate streams.

s: Which one of the following biotransformations provides maximum energy to the human body?
x: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is the high energy molecule that stores the energy. The conversion of ATP to ADP is an extremely crucial reaction for the supplying of energy for life processes. ATP hydrolysis is the final link between the energy derived from food or sunlight and useful work such as muscle contraction, the establishment of electrochemical gradients across the membrane and biosynthetic processes necessary to maintain life. ATP + H2O → ADP + Pi + energy 8. During respiration energy is produced in the form of : (a) ADP (b) ATP (c) NADP (d) CO2 U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2016 Ans. (b) Respiration is a set of metabolic reactions and processes that take place in the cells of organisms to convert biochemical energy from nutrients into Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP), and release waste products.

s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : During sleep, bright light is undesirable.
Reason (R) : In bright light, production of melatonin in the body is considerably increased. Select your answer using the codes given below.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not correct
x: Melatonin is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in the brain. It helps to regulate other hormones and maintains the body’s circadian rhythm. The circadian rhythm is an internal 24-hour ‘clock’ that plays a critical role at the time when we fall asleep and when we wake up. When it is dark, our body produces more melatonin. When it is bright, the production of melatonin drops. Clearly, the reason (R) is false, but assertion (A) is correct.

s: Insulin is produced by :
x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, not by the pituitary, thyroid or adrenal glands.

s: The pituitary gland by virtue of its tropic hormones controls the secretion activity of other endocrine glands. Which one of the following endocrine gland can function independent of the pituitary gland ?
x: The parathyroid glands are small endocrine glands in the neck of humans and other tetrapods that produce parathyroid hormone. Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin (one of the hormones made by the thyroid gland) have key roles in regulating the amount of calcium in the blood and within the bones. Parathyroid glands can function independent of the pituitary gland.

s: Which one of the following is a female sex-hormone?
x: Estrone is a weak postmenopausal estrogen and a minor female sex hormone. Estrogen (Oestrogen) is the actual female sex hormone. Testosterone is a male sex hormone which also includes Androgen. Thyroxine hormone is secreted the by thyroid gland which regulates the metabolism of the body.

s: In human body, Vitamin A is stored in –
x: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin that is stored in the liver, so the liver is the correct answer.

s: The kidneys in human beings are a part of system for
x: In humans, kidneys are the main organ of the excretion system. Filtering the blood and removing unnecessary and waste products from the body is the basic function of kidney.

s: In human body, which one of the following hormones regulates blood calcium and phosphate ?
x: Parathyroid hormone (PTH), secreted by the chief cells of the parathyroid glands, is a polypeptide containing 84 amino acids. Parathyroid hormone regulates serum calcium through its effects on the tissues. PTH reduces the reabsorption of phosphate from the proximal tubule of the kidney, which means more phosphate is excreted through in the urine.

s: Iodised salt is useful because it–
x: Iodised salt is table salt mixed with a minute amount of various salts of the element iodine. Iodine deficiency can cause thyroid gland problems. Iodised salt is useful as it controls the thyroid gland.

s: Where is urea separated from the blood?
x: The process, ultrafiltration occurs at the barrier between the blood and the filtrate in the renal capsule in the kidney. The kidneys remove urea and other toxic wastes from the blood, forming a dilute solution called urine in the process.

s: Which gland secretes the milk ejection hormone oxytocin?
x: The pituitary gland is called the master gland of the body which regulates the activities of all the internally secreting glands. Oxytocin is a mammalian neurohypophysial hormone, produced in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus by nerve axons and released by the posterior pituitary gland. Oxytocin acts primarily as a neuromodulator in the brain.

s: Which organ of the body is affected most on keeping fast for a long time ?
x: The kidneys are affected most on keeping fast for a longtime.

s: In human eye, image of object forms at :
x: The functioning of the human eye is similar to that of the photographic camera. The light rays travel into the cornea are refracted by the cornea and lens. In a normal eye, the image formed are transmitted from the retina to the brain along the optic nerve, where data processing takes place (the image is perceived the right way up).

s: If albumin is releasing with urine then the failure of which organ may occur?
x: In urine, there are about 91-96% water, about 2% unuseful salt ions, about 2.6% urea, about 0.3% creatinine and very small amount of uric acid and some other useless matter. The presence of albumin (a protein found in blood plasma) in it increases the chance of kidney failure.

s: Of the following which hormone is associated with ‘fight or flight’ concept ?
x: Adrenaline (Epinephrine) is commonly known as the 'fight or flight hormone'. Adrenaline is a hormone released from the adrenal glands and its major action together with noradrenaline is to prepare the body for fight or flight. Adrenaline causes dilation of blood vessels (vasodilation) which supply the brain, skeletal muscles, heart, lungs, liver, adipose tissues, sensory organs etc. Due to increased blood supply, these organs become very active and excited inducing alarm reaction, contraction of cardiac muscles, increasing both rate and force of heartbeat, pulse rate, arterial pressure and cardiac output. It produces a feeling of excitement.

s: Bright’s disease affects human body in the part –
x: Bright’s disease is a kidney disorder. In Bright’s disease, the blood vessels in the kidneys are inflamed and albumin is excreted in the urine. It is also known as nephritis and can be acute or chronic.

s: At the age of 20 years, the number of bones in human body is approximately-
x: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones, approximately 200, which is the case by about age 20.

s: Production of which one of the following is a function of the liver?
x: The liver is the largest gland in human body. It is located in the abdominal cavity, just below the diaphragm and has two lobes. It is an important digestive organ in human body. Its main function is the production of bile, storage of fat and conversion of harmful ammonia to urea (urea is one of the end products of protein metabolism that is excreted in the urine).

s: Which of the following is not correct regarding haemoglobin ?
o: It carries oxygen from lungs to cell.
It carries carbondioxide from tissues to lungs.
x: The notes do not cover this fact. Haemoglobin is the red, iron-containing pigment that carries O2 from lungs to tissues and also carries some CO2 back. It is not described as acidic, so option 3 is the incorrect statement.

s: Which of the following is not connective tissue?
x: Connective tissues include bone, cartilage and blood. Skeletal muscle is muscular tissue, not connective tissue.

s: Muscles are connected to bones by connective tissue called as
x: Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone, which is why option 2 is wrong.

s: Where is the governing centre of reflex action located?
x: A reflex action is coordinated by the spinal cord, so the response occurs without waiting for the brain. The cerebrum handles voluntary action.

s: Which of the following part of blood carry out the function of body defence?
x: White blood cells such as neutrophils defend the body against infection. Red cells carry oxygen and platelets help clotting.

s: The Human skeleton consists of
x: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones. 200 is only an approximation, so 206 is the exact answer.

s: Which of these bones is not a part of the human ear?
x: The ear ossicles are the malleus, incus and stapes. The femur is the thigh bone in the leg, not part of the ear.

s: In a healthy person, rate of heart beat in one minute is
x: The normal resting heart rate of a healthy adult is about 72 beats per minute.

s: The lens of the eye is behind the
x: Light enters through the pupil and then passes through the lens, so the lens lies just behind the pupil. The retina is at the back of the eye.

s: A person is unable to read a newspaper without his glasses. He is most probably suffering from
Which one of the following is an example of vestigial organ in man?
x: Ear muscles are vestigial in humans: they are reduced and functionless, though they are functional in other animals. Jaw, canine teeth and humerus are functional.

s: Retina of the eye is comparable to which of the following parts of a traditional camera?
x: The retina is the light-sensitive surface on which the image forms, like the film in a camera. The lens of the eye corresponds to the camera lens.

s: If father have blood group A and mother have blood group O, which one of following blood group may present in their son?
x: Mother O has genotype OO, and father A may be AO. The child can be A or O. Of the options, only O is possible; B and AB are impossible.

s: Which of the following roles is/are played by epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate in male reproductive system of human?
x: The epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate are accessory ducts and glands. They mature and carry sperms and provide fluid for motility. Spermatogenesis occurs only in the testes.

s:
Read the following statements and select the correct option. Statement I Active immunity is developed when a person’s own cells produce antibodies in response to infection or vaccine. Statement II Injection of snake anti-venom against snake bite is an example of active immunisation.
Codes
o: Both statements I and II are correct.
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.
Both statements I and II are incorrect.
x: Active immunity arises when the body's own cells make antibodies after infection or vaccination, so statement I is correct. Anti-venom gives ready-made antibodies, which is passive immunisation, so statement II is wrong.

s: Which one among the following is not correct about Down’s syndrome?
In female, a small portion of oviduct in removed and cut end is ligated by surgical operation is called
x: Tubectomy is the surgical cutting and ligation of the fallopian tube (oviduct) in females. Vasectomy is the male procedure on the vas deferens.

s: The ………… helps in equalising the pressure on either sides of the eardrum.
x: The eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the pharynx and equalises air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. Malleus and incus are ossicles that transmit vibrations.

s: Which one of the following is the special type of milk produced by a lactating mother, essential for the development of immune response of newborn body in human?
o: Breast milk produced after a month of childbirth
x: Colostrum is the first milk after childbirth. It is rich in antibodies and builds the newborn's immunity.

s: For a colourblind person, red colour appear as
x: Red-green colour blindness makes red look greenish or brownish; the notes do not cover it.

s: Which of the following natural substance contains iron (Fe) ?
x: Myoglobin is an iron-containing oxygen-storing protein in muscle. Chlorophyll contains magnesium, while collagen and carotene contain no iron.

s:
Oxygen transportation in a human body takes place through

I. Blood

II. Lungs

III. Tissue The correct sequence of transportation is
x: Oxygen enters the lungs first, is carried by the blood, and is then delivered to the tissues: lungs, blood, tissue.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Coronary artery supplies blood to heart muscles.

II. Pulmonary vein supplies blood to lungs.

III. Hepatic artery supplies blood to kidneys.

IV. Renal vein supplies blood to kidneys.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Only the coronary artery statement is correct. The pulmonary vein carries blood from the lungs to the heart, the renal artery supplies the kidneys, and the hepatic artery supplies the liver.

s:
Absorption of water in the human body can be found in

I. renal tubule in kidney

II. hepatic cells in liver

III. large intestine

IV. pancreatic duct
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Water is reabsorbed in the renal tubules and the large intestine. Hepatic cells and the pancreatic duct do not absorb water.

s:
With reference to the human body, consider the following statements.

I. The production of somatotropin goes up when a person exercises.

II. Men’s testes produces progesterone.

III. Women’s adrenal gland secrete testosterone.

IV. Stress causes the adrenals to release very less amount of cortisol than usual.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Somatotropin (growth hormone) rises with exercise, the testes make small amounts of progesterone, and the female adrenal secretes some testosterone, so I, II and III are correct. Stress raises cortisol, so IV is wrong.

s: In which medical condition is the eye’s optic nerve damaged and the condition worsens over time?
x: Glaucoma damages the optic nerve and worsens progressively, usually due to raised eye pressure. Cataract affects the lens.

s: The amount of which of the following component in the air does not change in the process of respiration?
x: Respiration changes the O2 (21% to 16%) and CO2 (0.04% to 4%) content of air, while nitrogen is not used and stays unchanged.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding haemoglobin is correct?
o: Haemoglobin present in RBCs can carry only oxygen, but not carbon dioxide.
Haemoglobin of RBC can carry both oxygen and carbon dioxide.
Haemoglobin of RBCs can carry only carbon dioxide.
Haemoglobin is only used for blood clotting and not for carrying gases.
x: Haemoglobin in RBCs carries mainly oxygen, and also some carbon dioxide (as carbamino-haemoglobin). It is not for clotting.

s: Which of the following cell secrete insulin?
x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas; alpha cells secrete glucagon.

s: Which one of the following salts is found in maximum amount in the human bones?
x: Bones consist mainly of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite), so it is the salt found in maximum amount.

s: A surge of which hormone stimulates ovulation in human females?
x: A mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone triggers ovulation.

s: Which of the following is the primary sex organ in females?
x: The ovary is the primary sex organ in females since it produces ova and hormones. The uterus, vagina and fallopian tube are accessory organs.

s: Which one of the following is not a component of human male reproductive system?
x: The cervix is part of the female reproductive system (the neck of the uterus). The urethra, seminal vesicle and vas deferens are in the male system.

s: By which combination of chromosome, a child will be male?
o: X from male and X from female
X from male and Y from female
Y from male and X from female
Y from male and Y from female
x: A male child is XY. The Y chromosome can only come from the father and the X from the mother.

s: Which among the following is the food tube?
x: The oesophagus is the food pipe carrying food from the pharynx to the stomach. The larynx is the voice box, the aorta is an artery and the thymus is a gland.

s: The saliva helps in the digestion of
x: Saliva contains salivary amylase, which begins the digestion of starch in the mouth.

s: The yellow colour of human urine is due to a pigment called
x: Urine is yellow due to the pigment urochrome, formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin.

s: Corpus luteum is a mass of cells found in
x: The corpus luteum forms in the ovary from the ruptured follicle after ovulation and secretes progesterone.

s: Tendons through which muscles are connected to bones are tightly compacted bundles of which one of the following long fibrous protein?
x: Tendons are made of collagen, a tough fibrous protein. Fibrin is for clotting, elastin is in elastic tissue and cellulose is not a protein.

s: With which of the physiological process, thrombin is associated?
x: Thrombin is the enzyme that converts fibrinogen to fibrin in blood clotting; the notes link clotting to vitamin K, but they do not mention thrombin, so the answer rests on general knowledge.

s: Person having blood group B can donate the blood to person having group
x: Group B donates to B and AB. AB is the universal recipient, so B can donate to AB. Group B cannot donate to A or O.

s: The oxygenated blood from the lungs in received by the
x: Oxygenated blood from the lungs returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium (auricle). The notes do not cover heart chambers.

s: Haemophilia is a genetic disorder which lead to
x: Haemophilia is a genetic disorder in which blood fails to clot because clotting factors are missing. The notes do not state this.

s: Which of the following is not a symptom of Wilson’s disease?
o: Problems with speech, swallowing or physical coordination.
Fluid build-up in the legs or abdomen
x: Wilson's disease is copper accumulation, causing neurological symptoms, liver problems and fluid build-up. Night blindness is caused by vitamin A deficiency, so it is not a symptom.

s: Which one of the following is an X-linked, recessive disorder caused by the deficiency of functional plasma clotting factor VIII (FVIII), which may be inherited or arise from spontaneous mutation?
x: Haemophilia A is the X-linked recessive disorder caused by a deficiency of clotting factor VIII. The others are blood cancers or a clotting disorder (thrombosis), not factor VIII deficiency.

s: ……… helps the eye to adjust the focal length of the lens.
x: The ciliary muscles of the ciliary body change the lens curvature and so adjust its focal length (accommodation). The notes do not cover this.

s: Bile is stored in
x: Bile is made in the liver but stored and concentrated in the gall bladder. The notes mention only that the liver produces bile.

s: In which organ of the human body are the lymphocytes cells formed?
x: Lymphocytes are formed from stem cells in the bone marrow of long bones. The notes do not state this.

s: Which chamber of human heart pumps fully oxygenated blood to the aorta and hence to the body?
x: The left ventricle has a thick wall and pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta for the whole body. The notes do not cover heart chambers.

s: Between which one of the following sets of bloods, in the transfusion possible?
x: AB is the universal recipient, so A can donate to AB. A cannot donate to O, B cannot donate to A, and AB cannot donate to O.

s: Which one among the following is the correct pathway for the elimination of urine?
x: Urine is made in the kidneys and passes through the ureters to the bladder, then out through the urethra. The notes mention only that the kidney filters urea.

s: Which one of following is smallest gland of body?
x: The pituitary is the smallest of the listed glands, about pea-sized. The notes call it the master gland but give no size.

s: Name the gland that controls the functioning of other endocrine glands
x: The pituitary is the master gland and controls other endocrine glands through hormones such as TSH and ACTH.

s: Which of the following gland is present between the lungs?
x: The thymus lies behind the sternum, between the lungs, and trains T cells. The pituitary and pineal glands are in the brain.

s: Which one of the following hormones do not contains peptide chain?
x: Cortisol is a steroid hormone from the adrenal gland, so it has no peptide chain. Oxytocin, corticotropin (ACTH) and insulin are peptide hormones.

s: Thyroid gland produces a hormone called ‘Thyroxine’ which
x: Thyroxine (T4) from the thyroid regulates the metabolic rate. Blood glucose is controlled by insulin, not thyroxine.

s: Cretinism is a human disorder which is due to the under secretin of
x: Cretinism results from thyroid hormone (thyroxine) deficiency, as stated for the thyroid in the notes.

s: Life saving hormone is
x: The adrenal gland is called life-saving because adrenaline and cortisol help the body cope with stress and emergencies. The notes list these hormones but do not use the phrase.

s: Which of the following hormone is called emergency hormone?
x: Adrenaline from the adrenal gland is the emergency hormone, used in fight-or-flight situations.

s: Which of the following is not a gland?
x: Gastrin is a hormone secreted by the stomach lining, not a gland. Thyroid, liver (the largest gland) and pancreas are all glands.

s: Which of the following gland is responsible for the secretion of insulin?
x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, so pancreas is correct.

s: Insulin is secreted by
x: Insulin comes from the Islets of Langerhans (beta cells) of the pancreas, not the spleen, gonads or liver.

s: Which of the following control blood pressure?
x: The adrenal glands secrete adrenaline and cortisol, which regulate blood pressure; parathyroid, thyroid and thymus do not primarily do so.

s: Which of the following endocrine glands in human is not found in pair?
x: The pituitary is a single gland at the base of the brain, while the adrenals, testes and ovaries occur in pairs.

s: A man suffering from diabetes mellitus drinks water more frequently as he has to eliminate from the blood extra
x: In diabetes mellitus blood glucose is high and excess glucose is excreted in urine, carrying water with it, so the person drinks more water to eliminate glucose.

s: Which of the following elements is needed in the human body to transfer electrical signals by nerve cells?
x: Sodium ions (Na+), with potassium, create the ion movements across nerve cell membranes that carry electrical signals. Lithium, rubidium and caesium are not needed for this.

s: Which of the following are the properties of neurons?
x: Neurons are specialised for excitability (responding to stimuli) and conductivity (transmitting impulses). Elasticity and flexibility are not their properties.

s: Rajat has hypermetropia. What type of lens will the ophthalmologist recommend to correct his vision?
x: Hypermetropia is corrected by a convex (converging) lens, while concave lenses correct myopia.

s: The human eye is like a camera and hence It contains a system of lens. The eye lens forms
o: a straight or upright, real image of the object on the retina.
an inverted virtual image of the object on the retina.
an inverted, real image of the object on the retina.
a straight or upright, real image of the object on the iris.
x: The eye lens acts like a convex lens in a camera and forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.

s: The pH of human’s slightly basic blood is normally around
x: Human blood is slightly alkaline, with a normal pH of about 7.35-7.45, so 7.5-8.0 is the closest option. Ranges below 7 would be acidic.

s: In an human brain memory power is found in
x: The cerebrum is the seat of memory, thinking and intelligence. The medulla and cerebellum control involuntary functions and balance.

s: Tachycardia is a condition characterised by
x: Tachycardia means an abnormally fast heart rate (above normal), whereas a slow rate is bradycardia.

s: The brain is responsible for
x: The brain handles thinking (cerebrum), heartbeat regulation (medulla) and body balance (cerebellum), so all of the above is correct.

s: Which of the following is not a part of the brain?
x: The pinna is the external part of the ear, not of the brain. Medulla, thalamus and pons are brain parts.

s: Largest part of human brain is
x: The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain, much larger than the cerebellum and medulla oblongata.

s: The focal length of the lens of a normal human eye is about
x: The eye lens forms images on the retina about 2.5 cm behind it, so the focal length of a normal eye is about 2.5 cm.

s: The change in focal length of an eye lens is caused by the action of the ……… .
x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens, which alters its focal length (accommodation). The pupil and iris control only the amount of light entering, and the retina receives the image.

s: Smooth muscles are likely to be found in
x: Smooth (involuntary) muscle is found in the walls of internal organs like the stomach. Leg and arm muscles are skeletal, and the heart has cardiac muscle.

s: After reaching the female genital tract, human sperms retain their fertilizing capacity for
x: Human sperms remain viable and capable of fertilising in the female genital tract for about one to two days.

s: The main thinking part of the brain is
x: The forebrain (cerebrum) is the seat of thinking, intelligence and memory, whereas the midbrain and hindbrain handle reflexes and coordination. The notes do not cover this.

s: Which of the following cells secrete androgen?
x: Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testes secrete androgens such as testosterone, while Sertoli cells nourish sperm. The notes only mention testes making testosterone in general.

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to human body.

I. The common bile duct releases its contents in stomach.

II. The pancreatic duct releases its contents into duodenum.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
x: The common bile duct and the pancreatic duct both open into the duodenum, not the stomach, so only statement II is correct.

s: In human body, what is the number of cervical vertebrae?
x: The human neck has 7 cervical vertebrae, the same number as in most mammals.

s: In human digestive system, the process of digestion starts in
x: Digestion starts in the buccal cavity, where salivary amylase begins breaking down starch. Protein digestion starts in the stomach, which is the tempting wrong option.

s: Which of the following is a vestigial organ?
x: The appendix is a vestigial organ with no significant function in humans. The heart, kidney and lungs are vital functioning organs.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding muscle contraction and relaxation is correct?
o: It involves movement of Zn+ + ion.
It involves Ca + + ion of blood.
It involves release of Ca + + from sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) and pumping Ca + + back in SR.
It involves exchange of Na and K.
x: Muscle contraction is triggered by Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and relaxation occurs when Ca2+ is pumped back into it. It does not depend on Ca2+ from the blood or on Zn.

s: Tooth enamel is made up of which one of the following calcium compounds?
x: Tooth enamel is mainly calcium phosphate in the form of hydroxyapatite, the hardest substance in the body.

o: increase in male but decrease in female
x: Narrower vessels increase resistance to blood flow, so blood pressure rises.

s: When kidneys fail to function, there is accumulation of
o: nitrogenous waste products in the blood.
x: The kidneys filter urea and other nitrogenous wastes out of the blood, so when they fail these wastes accumulate in the blood. This is why dialysis is needed.

s: Person who is colourblind can not distinguish between
x: The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.

s: A colour-blind person cannot differentiate between the colours
x: The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.

s: Which of the following is the first enzyme mixing with food in digestive region?
x: Food first meets salivary amylase in the mouth, which begins starch digestion. Pepsin acts in the stomach and trypsin in the intestine, so both come later.

s: Which among the following is not a connective tissue?
x: Blood, bone and cartilage are connective tissues. Skin is an organ made of epithelial and other tissues, not a connective tissue.

s: Which one of the following types of tissues will have contractile proteins?
x: Muscle tissue contains the contractile proteins actin and myosin, which produce contraction.

s: Buildup of which acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps?
x: During sudden strenuous activity muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up, causing cramps.

s: Sweat contains water and ………
x: Sweat is mostly water with dissolved salts (NaCl) and a little urea. Its salt content makes it taste salty.

s: Neutrophils and lymphocytes originate from
x: All blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, originate from stem cells in the bone marrow. Lymph nodes and the spleen only store or mature lymphocytes.

s: What is the name of the vessel that delivers the nutrient rich blood from the stomach and small intestine to the liver?
x: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the stomach and small intestine to the liver, so option 4 is right. The hepatic veins carry blood away from the liver, and the hepatic arteries supply it with oxygenated blood.

s: Which part of the body is responsible for the manufacture of red blood cells?
x: Red blood cells are made in the red bone marrow, so option 4 is right. The lungs, heart and brain do not make blood cells.

s: Which one of the following carries out the function in human beings similar to the one with Malpighian tubules perform in cockroaches and other insects?
x: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects, and the kidneys do the same job in humans by filtering waste such as urea from the blood.

s: Cerebrum is related to
x: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and controls thinking, memory and voluntary action. It is not part of the liver, heart or arteries.

s: Cartilage is not found in
x: The larynx, nose and external ear have cartilage in their walls. The urinary bladder is a muscular organ with no cartilage, so option 4 is right.
